sections.html:
A Rochester house is billed by Olmsted County. The county assessor decides what the property is worth for tax purposes, and one statement covers the levies of the county, the city, the schools and any special districts on your parcel.

Payments go to Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing at the Government Center, 151 4th Street SE, Rochester, MN 55904. Call 507-328-7636 about statements, 507-328-7635 about delinquent years, and 507-328-7670 for the assessor.

About 76,000 parcels countywide are valued as of each January 2, and state law ties the estimate to market value. Your value notice arrives in mid-March with the tax statement. The county's property assessments page covers the valuation side.

Rochester has 124,292 residents, the third largest city in Minnesota, and its housing market follows the medical economy around Mayo Clinic. The typical owner-occupied home was worth $310,500 for 2020 to 2024, and 65.1% of households own their homes. Median gross rent is $1,399, and median owner cost with a mortgage is $1,864 a month. Older stock near downtown and newer subdivisions on the edges price very differently, so a recent comparable sale matters more than a citywide median.

Owners pay in two installments, one in mid-May and one in mid-October. Farmland second halves and manufactured home second halves fall on November 15, and the manufactured home first half is due August 31.

If an installment is still open on your parcel, the penalty schedule in Minnesota Statutes 279.01 applies. Late fees start at 2 percent for a homestead and 4 percent for everything else, double once the next month begins, and then add 1 percent per month until they reach 8 percent (homestead) or 12 percent (other property).

Two details help when a payment is close to the line. Bills of $100 or under come due in one lump on May 15. And the statute gives a one-time break: a mailed check postmarked no more than one business day late can have its penalty erased, once per owner. If you mail near a deadline, ask a postal clerk for a hand-applied postmark.

Whichever method you choose, quote the parcel ID from your statement. A real property ID looks like RP 74.05.05.000000.

  • Online, on the county's property information site: card at 3.28 percent or e-check at $3.16, current year only, capped at $300,000. Allow seven to 10 business days for the bank to clear it and wait for the confirmation email.
  • Phone: 1-800-272-9829, jurisdiction number 3336. This line also takes back-year tax at the same rates.
  • Mail: check or money order made out to Olmsted County, with the stub, and five to seven business days of postal transit.
  • Counter: cash, check, money order or card at the Government Center, where cards add 2.15 percent. Drop boxes are there too.
  • Your bank's bill pay: the parcel ID serves as the account number, and the county counts the day it receives the money.

A free ACH withdrawal program is also available. Sign-up cutoffs come in April for the May draft and in September for the October draft, with money pulled on the 10th of May and October. Selling can end an enrollment, judged by the date the deed is recorded, so tell the office in writing if a sale lands near a withdrawal.

Begin with the assessor's office at 507-328-7670, carrying a recent appraisal or sale prices of comparable homes.

Still unsettled? Attend a meeting from the schedule on your valuation notice. Places with their own local board start there, and the rest go directly to the county board. By statute, local boards sit between April 1 and May 31 and can lower the assessor's overall total by no more than 1 percent. The county board follows in mid-June.

The last step is the Minnesota Tax Court, with a petition due by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A 2023 change also requires a copy to reach the county auditor. Olmsted County takes that copy by email at olmcotaxpetitionservice@olmstedcounty.gov or by hand at the County Attorney's Office. The Tax Court's phone number is 651-539-3260.

sections.h2: Relief programs that can lower your tax
sections.html:
State programs do most of the work. Homestead applications are due December 15 and exempt property applications February 1. Green Acres applications for farmland are due May 1.

  • Regular property tax refund, often called the circuit breaker, based on household income and the tax you pay.
  • Special refund, available when net tax rises by at least 12 percent and $100, with no income test. Both refunds use Form M1PR.
  • Senior citizen property tax deferral, applied for through the Minnesota Department of Revenue on Form CR-SCD.
  • Credit of $120 per month served for members of the military in a combat zone or hazardous duty area.

Notices of proposed taxes, the Truth in Taxation mailing, go out in mid-November. They project next year's bill if each taxing body adopts the budget now on the table, and they list hearing dates.

A past-due balance stays with the parcel, so ask the county for the exact payoff at 507-328-7635 before closing. Taxes left unpaid long enough can lead to forfeiture, with title passing to the State of Minnesota.

A sale also changes who gets the mail. The county sends one statement a year in late March, to the address you gave at closing, and sends none for mid-year purchases. Tax information may also show up in your closing papers. Once a deed is recorded, the assessor removes homestead status from the next assessment year unless the new owner applies and qualifies (Minnesota Statutes 272.115).

If your Rochester house has tax behind and you want a quick sale, pull together the parcel ID, your latest statement and the payoff figure first. If automatic withdrawal is on, send the county a written stop request, since a recorded transfer may end it only after the recording date. A buyer paying cash can close fast, but the payoff still has to be settled at the table.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Rochester, MN?
faqs.a: Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing takes the payments, and the county assessor sets values. For statement questions call 507-328-7636.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss the second-half Rochester property tax payment?
faqs.a: Penalties start at 2 percent for a homestead and 4 percent for other property, and they grow each month. Farm and manufactured home second halves are due November 15.

faqs.q: Can I pay Rochester property tax by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes. Card payments online or by phone add 3.28 percent, and an e-check adds $3.16. At the Government Center counter the card surcharge is 2.15 percent.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my Rochester tax statement?
faqs.a: Print one from the county's property information website or call 507-328-7636. Reprints at the office cost $2.

faqs.q: Does automatic withdrawal stop when I sell my Rochester home?
faqs.a: Not always right away. A transfer of the property may end the enrollment, but timing follows the recording date of the deed. Tell the county in writing if a withdrawal date is near.
